# kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1

A ClusterRoleBinding may be used to grant permission at the cluster level and in all namespaces

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `metadata` (Block List) (Required) Standard clusterRoleBinding's metadata. Exactly one `metadata` block must be present. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--metadata))
- `role_ref` (Block List) (Required) RoleRef references the Cluster Role for this binding. Exactly one `role_ref` block must be present. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--role_ref))
- `subject` (Block List) (Required) Subjects defines the entities to bind a ClusterRole to. At least one `subject` block must be present. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--subject))

### Optional

- `bootstrap_connection` (Block List, Max: 1) Connection settings used while this resource is being created, replacing the provider connection configuration in whole. After creation the provider connection configuration will be used. This is to support creating resources when the credentials are not available at plan time (e.g. when creating a cluster and configuring it in the same stack). For managing resources in multiple clusters use aliased providers instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--bootstrap_connection))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The name of the ClusterRoleBinding.

<a id="nestedblock--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Optional:

- `annotations` (Map of String) An unstructured key value map stored with the clusterRoleBinding that may be used to store arbitrary metadata. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations/
- `generate_name` (String) Prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique name ONLY IF the `name` field has not been provided. This value will also be combined with a unique suffix. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#idempotency
- `labels` (Map of String) Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) the clusterRoleBinding. May match selectors of replication controllers and services. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels/
- `name` (String) Name of the clusterRoleBinding, must be unique. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

Read-Only:

- `generation` (Number) A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state.
- `resource_version` (String) An opaque value that represents the internal version of this clusterRoleBinding that can be used by clients to determine when clusterRoleBinding has changed. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#concurrency-control-and-consistency
- `uid` (String) The unique in time and space value for this clusterRoleBinding. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#uids

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1" "example" {
  metadata {
    name = "terraform-example"
  }
  role_ref {
    api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
    kind      = "ClusterRole"
    name      = "cluster-admin"
  }
  subject {
    kind      = "User"
    name      = "admin"
    api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
  }
  subject {
    kind      = "ServiceAccount"
    name      = "default"
    namespace = "kube-system"
  }
  subject {
    kind      = "Group"
    name      = "system:masters"
    api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io"
  }
}
```

## Metadata and upgrades

Exactly one `metadata` block is required. RBAC names may contain colons, such as
`system:example`; they are not restricted to DNS names. Set either `name` or
`generate_name`, not both. Label and annotation values must be non-null strings;
omit an entry to remove it.

Upgrading SDKv2 state preserves the binding and its name-only ID. If configuration
explicitly sets `labels = {}` or `annotations = {}`, the first plan may show a
one-time in-place update because SDKv2 stored empty maps as null. The binding is
not replaced.

A `User` or `Group` subject with `api_group = ""` also shows a one-time in-place
update, displayed as `- api_group = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" -> null`. SDKv2
stored the API server's default instead of the configured `""`. Only Terraform
state changes; the binding is not modified or replaced. To avoid the update, omit
`api_group` or set it to `rbac.authorization.k8s.io`.

With Terraform 1.8 or later, migrate the deprecated resource name without
recreating the binding:

```terraform
moved {
  from = kubernetes_cluster_role_binding.example
  to   = kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.example
}
```

Change the corresponding resource declaration to `kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1`
and retain its configuration.

## Import

ClusterRoleBinding can be imported using the name, e.g.

```
$ terraform import kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.example terraform-name
```
